questions.question: Where do adjectives go in English?
options: At the end of the sentence
questions.explanation: English adjectives always come before the noun they describe: "a big house", "the red car".

questions.question: How do you form most adverbs from adjectives?
options: Adjectives and adverbs are always identical in English
questions.explanation: Most adverbs are formed by adding -ly to the adjective. Unlike Norwegian, English usually requires this change: "She sings beautifully", not "She sings beautiful".

questions.question: What is the comparative and superlative of the short adjective "tall"?
questions.explanation: Short adjectives (1-2 syllables) take -er and -est: tall, taller, tallest. Long adjectives use more/most.

questions.question: Which is the correct comparative form of "interesting"?
questions.explanation: Adjectives with three or more syllables use "more" for the comparative: "more interesting", "the most interesting".

questions.question: Which adverb does NOT take -ly?
questions.explanation: "Fast" is both adjective and adverb: "She runs fast." There is no word "fastly". "Quickly", "carefully" and "happily" all take -ly.
